P7628.corridor_notes: 16km branch entirely within Yi County (义县), Jinzhou, Liaoning — taps off the Panjin–Chifeng connector's Yixian distribution station and runs to a new Yixian East distribution station. One of 8 branches of the China–Russia Far East domestic-section Phase 3 (长春—石家庄天然气管道工程三阶段), approved per MEE批复 May 2026. Start and end resolve to the same county-level centroid — both stations are within Yi County but a finer township-level split point was not found in either source.
P7628.researcher_notes: Corroborated by 2 independent official sources: MEE EIA approval (2026-05, verbatim quotes 'gate: qi zi ... yi xian dong fen shu zhan, quan chang yue 16 gong li') and PipeChina's own EIA public-participation notice (2025-01), both give identical 16km length and matching station names.
P7628.blockers: Could not geocode the specific distribution stations at finer than county level — no township/village address found in source text or via Nominatim. Both endpoints currently share the same county-centroid coordinate; refine with a route map or as-built GIS if available.

P7629.corridor_notes: 136km connecting line runs from a new Laiyuan South junction station (on the Changchun–Shijiazhuang trunk, Laiyuan County, Baoding) southeast across Baoding prefecture to the existing Dingxing distribution station on the Mengxi coal-to-gas pipeline, in Dingxing County. DN1016mm, 10MPa design pressure per PipeChina notice.
P7629.researcher_notes: Two independent official sources (MEE approval + PipeChina EIA notice) agree exactly on 136km length and both station names.
P7629.blockers: County-level precision only; exact station coordinates for 涞源南联络站 and 定兴分输站 not found in open sources.

P7630.corridor_notes: 470km branch, the longest of Phase 3 — runs from Zhangbei distribution station (tied to Shaanxi–Beijing Line IV) east across northern Hebei (Zhangjiakou → Chengde prefectures) to a new Kuancheng terminal station in Kuancheng Manchu Autonomous County. DN508mm, 10MPa. Feeds the Xinglong (P7631) and Pingquan (P7632) branches partway along its route.
P7630.researcher_notes: 2 independent official sources, exact length match (470km).

P6679.corridor_notes: GEM's OtherLanguageAlternativePipelineNames field labels this cancelled 8.8km row '陕京四线联络线' (Shaan-Jing Line IV connecting line). The only officially documented connector matching this description is a ~1km tie-in built as part of the Changchun–Shijiazhuang Phase 2 trunk, linking the trunk's Zhangjiakou West compressor station (万全区) to Shaan-Jing Line IV — see PipeChina's Phase-2 EIA notice ('张家口与陕京四线联通，新建1km管道'). That figure (~1km) does not match GEM's recorded 8.8km, so this GEM row may be either (a) a stale/superseded entry from an earlier route concept later replaced by the shorter Phase-2 tie-in, or (b) a distinct, still-unbuilt longer connector this research could not independently locate. Treating Zhangjiakou West compressor station as the one confidently-sourced anchor point; the far/tie-in endpoint at 8.8km distance is NOT independently confirmed.
P6679.researcher_notes: Only 1 source found describing a Shaan-Jing IV connector in this corridor (PipeChina Phase-2 EIA notice), and its stated length (~1km) conflicts with GEM's 8.8km — falls short of the 2-independent-source / length-corroboration bar. Recommend review of whether this cancelled row should be retired as superseded by the Phase-2 trunk's built-in tie-in, since no separate 8.8km project could be found in current planning documents.
P6679.blockers: No source independently confirms an 8.8km Shaan-Jing IV connecting line distinct from the ~1km Phase-2 tie-in; could not locate the far/tie-in endpoint. Web search was constrained mid-session (WebSearch tool quota exhausted; Bing/Baidu/Google/DuckDuckGo returned no usable results via WebFetch, eiafans.com unreachable).

P6680.corridor_notes: GEM's alternative name '顺平—定兴联络线' (Shunping–Dingxing connecting line) suggests an early/superseded corridor concept reaching the same Dingxing distribution station as the current, officially documented 涞源—定兴联络线 (Laiyuan–Dingxing, P7629, 136km) — but via a different county (Shunping instead of Laiyuan) and a shorter length (99.5km vs 136km). No source describing a Shunping-routed corridor could be found; it may be a pre-restructuring alignment abandoned when the project was finalized via Laiyuan. Both Shunping and Dingxing are real Baoding-prefecture counties (Nominatim-confirmed) but the specific pipeline claim is unsourced for Shunping.
P6680.researcher_notes: Likely an earlier alternate-routing concept for what became P7629 (same eventual Dingxing terminus, different starting county, different length) — flagging the relationship for review rather than setting duplicate_of, since status/length differ and no source confirms they are literally the same planned asset.
P6680.blockers: No independent source found for a 'Shunping–Dingxing' gas connecting line at any length; GEM's own field is the only occurrence. Web search was constrained (WebSearch quota exhausted; alternate search engines via WebFetch/curl returned no usable results — Bing served unrelated cached pages, Baidu CAPTCHA-blocked, Google blocked, eiafans.com unreachable).

P6681.corridor_notes: GEM's alternative name '鄂安沧联络线' (E'an-Cang connecting line) matches an officially documented ~0.1km tie-in between the Changchun–Shijiazhuang trunk's Luquan East compressor station and the adjacent Ordos–Anping–Cangzhou pipeline's Luquan distribution/pigging station (both in Luquan District, Shijiazhuang) — PipeChina Phase-2 EIA notice states the two stations are built adjacent to one another ('鹿泉东压气站与鄂安沧管道鹿泉分输清管站邻建'). GEM's recorded 3.5km length does not match the ~0.1km official figure, so as with P6679 this may be a stale/superseded entry from an earlier concept.
P6681.researcher_notes: Length mismatch (3.5km GEM vs ~0.1km official current tie-in) — same pattern as P6679. Recommend review of both for possible retirement as superseded entries; the current Phase-2 trunk EIA describes both connectors as essentially co-located station pairs, not multi-km lines.
P6681.blockers: No source describing a distinct 3.5km E'an-Cang connecting line was found; only the ~0.1km adjacent-station tie-in is documented. Search engines largely inaccessible this session (see P6679 blockers).
